subject: chemistry-hl
about: Original practice questions written for the IB Chemistry 2025 guide (HL). Not IB past-paper questions or markschemes, and not a prediction of exam questions. Calculator-free practice: every item can be done without a calculator.

items.topicLabel: R1.1 Measuring enthalpy changes
items.stem: Which process is exothermic?

items.topicLabel: R1.1 Measuring enthalpy changes
items.stem: 100 g of water is heated by 10 K. Using c = 4.2 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹, how much heat is absorbed?

items.topicLabel: R1.1 Measuring enthalpy changes
items.stem: On an energy profile, what represents ΔH?

items.topicLabel: R1.2 Energy cycles in reactions
items.stem: Using bond enthalpies H–H 436, Cl–Cl 242, H–Cl 431 kJ mol⁻¹, what is ΔH for H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl?

items.topicLabel: R1.2 Energy cycles in reactions
items.stem: Which equation represents ΔHf⦵ of water?
items.note: One mole of product from elements in standard states.

items.topicLabel: R1.2 Energy cycles in reactions
items.stem: A → B ΔH = +50; B → C ΔH = −80 kJ mol⁻¹. What is ΔH for C → A?
items.note: A → C = −30, so the reverse is +30.

items.topicLabel: R1.2 Energy cycles in reactions
items.stem: Which step in a Born–Haber cycle is always exothermic?
items.note: Adding an electron to a Cl atom releases energy.

items.topicLabel: R1.3 Energy from fuels
items.stem: Which product shows incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon?

items.topicLabel: R1.3 Energy from fuels
items.stem: What is the balanced equation's O₂ coefficient for complete combustion of ethanol?

items.topicLabel: R1.3 Energy from fuels
items.stem: Which fuel is renewable?

items.topicLabel: R1.4 Entropy and spontaneity (additional higher level)
items.stem: Which change has the largest increase in entropy?
items.note: Liquid to gas is the biggest increase in dispersal.

items.topicLabel: R1.4 Entropy and spontaneity (additional higher level)
items.stem: A reaction has ΔH = −50 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS = −100 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. When is it spontaneous?
items.note: ΔG < 0 while TΔS (in kJ) is smaller than 50, i.e. T < 500 K.

items.topicLabel: R1.4 Entropy and spontaneity (additional higher level)
items.stem: What does ΔG⦵ > 0 tell you about K?
items.note: ΔG⦵ = −RT ln K, so ln K < 0.

items.topicLabel: R2.1 How much? The amount of chemical change
items.stem: What is the coefficient of O₂ when C₂H₆ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O is balanced with whole numbers?

items.topicLabel: R2.1 How much? The amount of chemical change
items.stem: 0.20 mol H₂ reacts with 0.20 mol O₂: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Which is limiting, and how much H₂O forms?

items.topicLabel: R2.1 How much? The amount of chemical change
items.stem: Which reaction type always has 100% atom economy?
items.note: All reactant atoms end up in the single product.

items.topicLabel: R2.2 How fast? The rate of chemical change
items.stem: Why does a powder react faster than a lump of the same mass?

items.topicLabel: R2.2 How fast? The rate of chemical change
items.stem: What does a catalyst change?

items.topicLabel: R2.2 How fast? The rate of chemical change
items.stem: Rate = k[X][Y]². What happens to the rate if both [X] and [Y] double?

items.topicLabel: R2.2 How fast? The rate of chemical change
items.stem: Which units are correct for k in rate = k[A]?

items.topicLabel: R2.3 How far? The extent of chemical change
items.stem: What is the expression for K for H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)?

items.topicLabel: R2.3 How far? The extent of chemical change
items.stem: For an exothermic forward reaction, what happens to K when temperature rises?

items.topicLabel: R2.3 How far? The extent of chemical change
items.stem: K for A ⇌ B is 4. What is K for B ⇌ A?

items.topicLabel: R2.3 How far? The extent of chemical change
items.stem: Which change shifts N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g) to the right?
items.note: Fewer moles on the left; lower pressure favours more moles.
